title: Resilient Usage Envelope Adapter with Probabilistic Field Repair
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The console analytics pipeline receives events from multiple SDKs (JS/Go/Python), hosted paths, and partner integrations. Currently incoming envelopes vary in field names, nesting, and optionality; strict schema rejection causes data loss and customer confusion. Goal: implement a resilient ingestion adapter that normalizes disparate envelopes into a canonical event shape, applies lightweight probabilistic repair for missing or malformed non-sensitive fields, and provides explicit validation outcomes for downstream consumers and dashboards.

Scope: backend service in the console ingestion tier that runs after transport-level de-duplication and auth checks, before the streaming validator and long-term storage. It must 1) resolve schema version metadata, 2) normalize field aliases and case conventions, 3) apply deterministic transforms (timestamp parsing, numeric coercion), 4) attempt probabilistic repair when safe, 5) annotate events with a compact validation trace, and 6) emit metrics and change events for schema drift.

Key constraints and non-goals: Repair logic must never infer or surface sensitive PII. We will not perform heavy ML model inference at ingest (no large model calls) — repair will be lightweight classifier/heuristic based and run inline with bounded latency. The adapter must preserve a provenance header so reprocessing/replay can revert repairs if a downstream schema migration rolls back.

High-level design: The adapter is a horizontally scalable stateless service implemented in Go. Components:
- Schema registry client: resolves canonical schema and alias maps per event type/version.
- Alias/Normalization layer: maps incoming keys using fuzzy-match rules + curated alias list stored in the registry.
- Deterministic transformers: timestamps, enum normalization, numeric coercion, flattened nested fields for analytics.
- Probabilistic repair module: a small decision-tree ensemble (Go-encoded) that returns a repair candidate + confidence. Repairs are applied only when confidence >= threshold and field is non-security-critical.
- Validation trace: structured string tags and a compact JSON string that fits inside a single header field (for routing/observability) describing applied transforms, repairs, and final schema version.
- Emission: validated/normalized event forwarded to the streaming validator topic (Kafka) and a side-topic for low-confidence repairs for offline review.

Operational requirements: 99th percentile additional ingest latency < 8ms; validation error rate (hard rejects) reduced by at least 40% for SDK traffic; metrics exposed per event-type: normalized_count, repaired_count, repair_confidence_histogram, reject_count, avg_latency_ms. Must integrate with existing console Console-Observability dashboards and alerting (SLOs on error budget).

Rollout plan: Canary with 1% traffic (internal orgs) -> 10% with read-only side-channel for low-confidence repairs -> 50% with auto-apply for high-confidence -> global. Reprocess path: maintain provenance to selectively re-run repair logic if schema registry updates.

Why different from previous validators: instead of rejecting or pausing ingestion on schema drift, this adapter focuses on safe, auditable normalization and measured repair so product teams keep analytics continuity while liminal schema issues are surfaced and owned.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming SDK events are normalized to the canonical envelope for >= 90% of cases in test harness
Probabilistic repairs applied only when confidence >= 0.92 for critical metrics fields and >= 0.8 for non-critical fields
Side-topic captures 100% of low-confidence repairs for offline review
End-to-end additional latency introduced by adapter median < 3ms and 99th < 8ms under p95 load
Validation trace header present on every emitted event and viewable in Console-Observability
decisions: Implement adapter as a separate stateless service in Go to match ingest runtime and simplify autoscaling
Use a lightweight decision-tree ensemble serialized into Go for probabilistic repair (no external model calls) to keep latency predictable
Repair only non-PII and non-auth fields; always annotate provenance and confidence
Emit low-confidence repairs to a dedicated Kafka topic for human/ML review and offline model retraining
next_steps: Prototype alias matching and deterministic transformers using existing alias maps (ENG-50312)
Define repair feature set and train small classifier on historical telemetry samples (privacy-scrubbed)
Implement schema registry client and alias table APIs with caching TTLs
Add metrics and trace fields; create Console-Observability dashboards and SLOs before canary
Write integration tests and load tests simulating mixed SDK traffic and partner payloads
